facts.content: Patient presents with left elbow swelling for approximately one week.
facts.source_text: CC: L elbow swelling x ~1 wk

facts.content: The left elbow swelling is painless and mildly warm with a fluid-like feel.
There was no trauma preceding the left elbow swelling and no prior episodes.
Patient has a history of osteoarthritis diagnosed by their general practitioner a few years ago.
facts.source_text: PMH: OA dx by GP (few yrs ago)

facts.content: Patient is not taking any current medications.
Ibuprofen 400 mg three times daily with food over the counter was recommended, with instructions to stop if heartburn occurs.
facts.source_text: Ibuprofen 400 mg TID with food (OTC); stop if heartburn

facts.content: Patient is allergic to peanuts.
Patient reports no known drug allergies.
Patient reports no known family history of rheumatologic disease but is unsure.
facts.source_text: FH: no known rheum dz (pt unsure)

facts.content: Patient works at a desk job.
Patient runs two to three times per week.
Left elbow swelling is assessed as consistent with olecranon bursitis, atraumatic with mild warmth and minimal tenderness, and there is currently low concern for septic arthritis.
facts.source_text: 1) L elbow swelling c/w olecranon bursitis; atraumatic, mild warmth, minimal tenderness; low concern for septic arthritis currently

facts.content: Osteoarthritis is noted by history.
Peanut allergy is listed as an assessment item.
Ordered laboratory tests including inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and urate, with test forms to be sent to the patient.
facts.source_text: Labs: inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheum Abs, urate; send test forms to pt

facts.content: Laboratory results are expected approximately five to six days after the blood draw.
Follow-up after labs will be by phone, video, or in-person according to patient preference.
facts.source_text: F/U after labs via phone/video or in-person per pt preference

facts.content: Safety-net advice was given to seek urgent review if there is increased erythema, severe pain, or spreading redness of the elbow.
facts.source_text: Safety net: seek urgent review if ↑erythema, severe pain, spreading redness

facts.content: Osteoarthritis is to be monitored.
Patient was advised to avoid peanuts due to allergy.
Video examination shows visible left elbow swelling with dry skin at the olecranon tip.
facts.source_text: Video exam: visible L elbow swelling; skin dry at olecranon tip

facts.content: The left elbow is warmer than the adjacent skin.
There is no tenderness at the olecranon tip but mild tenderness adjacent to the swelling on self-palpation.
facts.source_text: Non-tender at tip; mild tenderness adjacent to swelling on self-palpation

facts.content: The patient reports a fluctuant feel of the left elbow swelling on palpation.
facts.source_text: Pt reports fluctuant feel on palpation

facts.content: Follow-up is planned after laboratory testing via phone, video, or in-person based on patient preference.
facts.source_text: F/U after labs via phone/video or in-person per pt preference
